payload.title: Getting Married in Italy as an Australian
payload.primary_keyword: getting married in italy as an australian
payload.audience: Australian couples in their 30s, affluent, wedding budget about AUD 130k
payload.reader: An Australian couple in their 30s who have settled on Italy, are 9 to 18 months out with about AUD 130k to spend, and need to know exactly which documents to get in Australia, which in Italy, in what order and how long before the date, so their marriage is legally valid and recognised when they fly home.
payload.goal: Speak with a Wedded Advisor about the legal and paperwork side of an Italian wedding (Wedded Concierge consultation).
payload.angle: Most page-one results are written for UK or US couples and talk about a Certificate of No Impediment. This is the Australian version: the Nulla Osta issued by the Australian Embassy in Rome or the Consulate-General in Milan, what you prepare before leaving Australia (apostilles from DFAT, certified Italian translations), a working-back timeline from your date, the real choice between civil, religious and symbolic ceremonies, and what happens with your Italian marriage certificate once you are home in Australia.
must_include: The Nulla Osta for Australians: what it is, that it comes from the Australian Embassy in Rome or the Consulate-General in Milan (not a UK-style CNI), who must appear and how it is booked [[VERIFY: current Embassy/Consulate process, appointment rules and whether both partners attend]]

Documents to prepare in Australia: birth certificates, proof of identity, evidence of divorce or death of a former spouse where relevant, DFAT apostilles and certified Italian translations [[VERIFY: current document list and apostille requirements for Italy]]

Steps in Italy in order: Nulla Osta, legalisation at the Prefettura where required, Declaration of Intent (Dichiarazione di Matrimonio) at the comune, then the ceremony with an interpreter if needed [[VERIFY: Prefettura step and any waiting period for foreign nationals]]
A working-back timeline from the wedding date, starting in Australia (as a table), with any time figure sourced or marked [[VERIFY]]
Civil vs religious (Catholic concordat) vs symbolic ceremony: legal effect, venue limits for civil ceremonies, and the option to marry legally in Australia and hold a symbolic ceremony in Italy

Recognition back home: how an overseas marriage is treated under Australian law and what certificate to bring home [[VERIFY: Marriage Act 1961 recognition of foreign marriages and any registration step]]
Same-sex couples: civil union (unione civile) in Italy versus marriage, and how it is treated in Australia [[VERIFY: current Italian law and Australian recognition]]
Fees stated only as 'a fee applies' unless a current official source gives the amount; link to the general legal guide for non-Australian detail instead of repeating it
avoid: Calling the Australian document a Certificate of No Impediment, or copying UK steps from /expert-advice/how-do-british-citizens-get-married-in-italy
Repeating the general legal guide section by section; summarise in one line and link to it
Any fee, processing time or waiting period not traced to an official source (Embassy, DFAT, comune or Prefettura)
Legal advice framing: say what the process is and that rules change, and point readers to the Embassy for confirmation
Business details not yet confirmed: Concierge fee model, deposits, From AUD price ranges, Wedded Privileges detail, a named Advisor, real weddings
Competitor wording, claims or images (including Easy Weddings)
Stacked superlatives, exclamation marks, em dashes, US spelling
payload.cannibalisation_check: Overlap found. (1) /expert-advice/getting-married-in-italy-the-complete-legal-guide-for-destination-couples targets the same head keyword as a general, nationality-neutral legal guide, and is duplicated at the root URL /getting-married-in-italy-the-complete-legal-guide-for-destination-couples. (2) /expert-advice/how-do-british-citizens-get-married-in-italy is the UK version (CNI route). (3) /how-do-you-get-a-lake-como-wedding (also listed under /expert-advice/) is titled 'Lake Como Wedding: Legal Guide to Marrying in Italy'. (4) /how-to-plan-a-destination-wedding-in-italy-if-youre-overseas covers overseas planning generally. How this differs: this post is the Australian-specific legal guide (Nulla Osta from the Australian Embassy or Consulate, DFAT apostilles, timeline from Australia, recognition at home) and links to the general guide for everything else. Recommendation: keep the general /expert-advice/ guide on the global head keyword 'getting married in italy' and re-title it around 'legal requirements for foreigners'; this post targets the head keyword for Australian searchers with the modifiers 'as an Australian' / 'Australians' in title, H1 and meta, with au_focus scope. Separately, 301 the root duplicate to the /expert-advice/ URL and give the Lake Como page a Lake Como-specific title so three pages stop competing. The SEO researcher should confirm with AU vs global SERP data on the second pass; the redirects and re-titles are a human decision.
